original.target_description: Condition 1 self-enacted unfair task assignment versus Condition 2 observing another person make the same unfair assignment, after Condition 1 altruist/randomizer exclusions; fairness judgments. Conditions identified from Method and Results narrative, not numeric matching.

n.sample_role: Participants in the Condition 1 versus Condition 2 comparison; analytic count not established.
n.exclusions: Two Condition 1 subjects excluded for acting altruistically or using the randomizer; separate counts for these exclusion reasons are not supplied.
n.location: pp. 689–690, Method and Results and Discussion
n.quote: Seventy-six subjects were randomly assigned to one of four ... Two subjects in Condition 1 were removed from analysis for ... acting altruistically or using the randomizer; all others assigned ... themselves to the green condition.

es.location: p. 690, Results and Discussion and Figure 1 caption
es.quote: planned contrast (with contrast weights of 1, !1, 1, and !1 for ... Conditions 1 through 4, respectively) confirmed the existence of ... hypocrisy at both the individual and the group levels, F(1, 72) 5 ... 11.75, p 5 .001, prep 5 .99, d 5 1.11.

notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is a complete two-page Short Report titled Moral Hypocrisy, subtitle Social Groups and the Flexibility of Virtue, by Piercarlo Valdesolo and David DeSteno, Psychological Science Volume 18 Number 8, pp. 689–690, copyright 2007. This matches the neutral original reference and is primary Methods/Results text; DOI is not printed in the supplied text. No PDF was supplied. Assigned fields only: n_o and es_value_o. The self/other target is located independently through the Condition 1 and Condition 2 procedures and the individual-level narrative. No condition-specific final sample counts are supplied. Seventy-six is whole-study random assignment across four conditions; subtracting two exclusions would not establish the assigned two-condition comparison N, and no df-based N is used. Printed candidate d 1.11 accompanies the planned contrast across Conditions 1 through 4 with weights 1, -1, 1, -1; it is not a separately printed self-versus-other d and is therefore not assigned to es.value. Figure 1 supplies shared pairwise bounds (ts > 2.08, ps < .05, preps > .89), without a pair-specific d. No conversions performed. Unassigned p, replication, and reported_success are null placeholders, not findings.
